rationale: The paper reports a small-molecule homogeneous organic reaction: photocatalytic [2+1] cycloaddition of phenylacetylene with difluoroacetylsilane followed by acid-catalyzed methanol functionalization to give difluoromethyl cyclopropenyl ethers. The authors performed and reported DFT calculations directly on the methanol addition step to cyclopropenium intermediates and on relative Gibbs free energies of the possible methoxy cyclopropene regioisomers. These computations address the observed regioselectivity and isomer equilibration, so they can serve as private evaluation references. The public question is reframed to ask why the reaction is regioselective under the stated conditions, without giving the authors' selected transition state, mechanistic explanation, or computed energy values.

source_quotes.quote: At the outset, we explored the reactions of difluoroacetylsilanes and alkynes for the synthesis of difluoromethyl-substituted alkoxyl cyclopropenes, because no general method currently exists for the synthesis of these compounds. After extensive investigation of reaction conditions (for details, see Table 1), we found that when the mixture of alkyne 1a and 1.5 equivalents of difluoroacetylsilane 2a and 1.5 mol% of photocatalyst 4CzIPN (2,4,5,6- tetra(9H-carbazol-9-yl)isophthalonitrile) was irradiated under blue LEDs (6 W, 460 nm) in DCM (di-chloromethane) for 12 h, the corresponding [2 + 1] cycloaddition product A was formed (82% isolated yield, Table 1, entry 1). Subsequent investigation of the ratio of 1a/2a, the amount of MeOH and TMSCl (chlorotrimethylsilane) led to the finding the synthesis of the desired cyclopropene 3a (Table 1, entries 1–11), with an optimal yield of 83% (Table 1, entry 10). It was found that the silyl group significantly influenced the reaction and the SiPhMe<sub>2</sub>-containing difluoroacetylsilane 2a gave the best yield of 3a (83% isolated yield with >20:1 regioisomer ratios [r.r.]; Table 1, entry 10), and the more sterically hindered SiPh and SiEt groups decreased the efficiency of the reactions (Table 1, entries 12 and 13). Without TMSCl, compound A was stable in MeOH, and no conversion to compound 3a was found in 5 min (Table 1, entry 14).

Mechanistically, the formation of aromatic cyclopropenium cations from the [2 + 1] cycloaddition products under acidic conditions appears to be reasonable (Figure 4A). Cyclopropenium cations are known to be relatively stable intermediates due to their aromaticity and the stabilizing effects of the positive charge delocalized over the ring.<sup>25–30</sup> However, the equilibrium among multiple π-type cyclopropenium cations would pose a significant challenge in achieving selectivity control during subsequent reactions with MeOH. Interestingly, the reaction between 1a and 2a showed excellent regioselectivity and the regioisomer 3a<sup>′</sup> was only obtained in 2% yield, without the observation of regioisomer 3a<sup>′′</sup> (3a, 1.61 g, 82% yield, Figure 4B). In order to understand the origin of regioselectivity of the reaction, we performed density functional theory (DFT) calculations on the nucleophilic addition step (Figure 4A). Our results indicate that methanol nucleophilic addition to the cyclopropenium cation intermediate occurs preferentially at the carbon atom adjacent to the difluoromethyl group. In the transition state TS-1, a hydrogen bonding is formed between the OH group of methanol and the F atom of the difluoromethyl group. This hydrogen bonding stabilizes the transition state TS-1, resulting in the lowest activation energy. In contrast, the other two transition states TS-1<sup>′</sup> and TS-1<sup>′′</sup> have higher free energy barriers due to steric repulsion between the methyl and phenyl groups (for details, see Figure S9). Furthermore, we also investigated the stability of the three possible isomers and found that the Gibbs free energy of compound 3a was 3.2 kcal/mol lower than that of 3a<sup>′</sup>, and 7.2 kcal/mol lower than that of 3a<sup>′′</sup>, indicating that compound 3a is the thermodynamically most-stable isomer. This calculation result is consistent to the experimental study that 3a<sup>′</sup> was converted to 3a in 91% yield when 3a<sup>′</sup> was subjected to MeOH in the presence of 5 mol % of TMSCl, indicating the equilibrium of 3a, 3a<sup>′</sup>, and 3a<sup>′′</sup> under the reaction conditions (Figure 4A). Moreover, the gas chromatography (GC) analysis of the unpurified reaction mixture of 1a and 2a confirmed the formation of PhSiMe<sub>2</sub>SiOSiMe<sub>2</sub>Ph in 71% yield and PhSiMe<sub>2</sub>OMe in 10% yield (Figure 4A), which accounts for the efficient ether transfer reaction with only 3.0 equivalents of MeOH. The formation of strong Si–O bond is probably a driving force of the reaction, indicating the importance of using acylsilanes as the carbynyl cation equivalents (for the proposed more detailed mechanism, see Figure S8). We propose that the intermediates 3a and 3a<sup>′</sup> are more stable than \pmb { 3 } \mathbf { a } ^ { \prime \prime } due to the conjugation between the phenyl group and the C=C bond. The lower stability of 3a<sup>′</sup> compared with 3a might be due to the fact that when an electron-withdrawing group (EWG) is directly attached to the C=C bond, it can decrease the electron density, thereby weakening the strength of the π bond.<sup>24</sup>

In an argon-filled glovebox, a flame-dried screw-cap reaction tube equipped with a magnetic stir bar was charged with 4CzIPN (2.4 mg, 3 μmol, 1.5 mol %), 1a (20.4 mg, 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv.) and dry DCM (1.0 mL), and 2a (64.2 mg, 0.3 mmol, 1.5 equiv.) sequentially. The tube was sealed with a screw cap equipped with a septum, removed from the glovebox, and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature (RT) for 12 h under blue LEDs (6 W, 460 nm). Then ROH (0.6 mmol, 3.0 equiv.) and TMSCl (1.1 mg, 0.01 mmol, 5 mol %) were added. The reaction mixture was stirred at RT for 5 min. The reaction mixture was concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude product was purified with column chromatography on silica gel (200–300 mesh) to afford the title compound.

All DFT calculations were performed using the Gaussian 16 series of programs <sup>[s9]</sup>. The M06-2X exchange-correlation functional <sup>[s10]</sup> was used for all DFT calculations, solvent effects of dichloromethane were considered in geometric optimizations with the SMD solvent model <sup>[s11]</sup>, and under this protocol, the structures of the intermediates and transition states were optimized and characterized by frequency analyses using a 6 { - } 3 1 1 { + } \mathrm { G } ( \mathrm { d } , \mathsf { p } ) <sup>[s12-s13]</sup> basis set for all atoms. Vibrational frequency calculations were performed for all stationary points to confirm if each optimized structure is a local minimum. All minima (intermediates) have no imaginary frequencies, and all optimized transition state structures have only one imaginary (negative) frequency.

scientific_question: For the acid-promoted methanol functionalization of the difluoromethyl phenylcyclopropenium intermediate generated from phenylacetylene and difluoroacetylsilane in dichloromethane, what factors control the observed regioselectivity of methoxy cyclopropene formation?
computation_relevance: The authors' DFT calculations were performed on the nucleophilic addition step of methanol to the cyclopropenium cation intermediate and on the relative Gibbs free energies of the possible methoxy cyclopropene isomers. These results directly support evaluation of regioselectivity and relative product stability for the selected reaction phenomenon.

source_quotes.quote: At the outset, we explored the reactions of difluoroacetylsilanes and alkynes for the synthesis of difluoromethyl-substituted alkoxyl cyclopropenes, because no general method currently exists for the synthesis of these compounds. After extensive investigation of reaction conditions (for details, see Table 1), we found that when the mixture of alkyne 1a and 1.5 equivalents of difluoroacetylsilane 2a and 1.5 mol% of photocatalyst 4CzIPN (2,4,5,6- tetra(9H-carbazol-9-yl)isophthalonitrile) was irradiated under blue LEDs (6 W, 460 nm) in DCM (di-chloromethane) for 12 h, the corresponding [2 + 1] cycloaddition product A was formed (82% isolated yield, Table 1, entry 1). Subsequent investigation of the ratio of 1a/2a, the amount of MeOH and TMSCl (chlorotrimethylsilane) led to the finding the synthesis of the desired cyclopropene 3a (Table 1, entries 1–11), with an optimal yield of 83% (Table 1, entry 10). It was found that the silyl group significantly influenced the reaction and the SiPhMe<sub>2</sub>-containing difluoroacetylsilane 2a gave the best yield of 3a (83% isolated yield with >20:1 regioisomer ratios [r.r.]; Table 1, entry 10), and the more sterically hindered SiPh and SiEt groups decreased the efficiency of the reactions (Table 1, entries 12 and 13). Without TMSCl, compound A was stable in MeOH, and no conversion to compound 3a was found in 5 min (Table 1, entry 14).

In an argon-filled glovebox, a flame-dried screw-cap reaction tube equipped with a magnetic stir bar was charged with 4CzIPN (2.4 mg, 3 μmol, 1.5 mol %), 1a (20.4 mg, 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv.) and dry DCM (1.0 mL), and 2a (64.2 mg, 0.3 mmol, 1.5 equiv.) sequentially. The tube was sealed with a screw cap equipped with a septum, removed from the glovebox, and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature (RT) for 12 h under blue LEDs (6 W, 460 nm). Then ROH (0.6 mmol, 3.0 equiv.) and TMSCl (1.1 mg, 0.01 mmol, 5 mol %) were added. The reaction mixture was stirred at RT for 5 min. The reaction mixture was concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude product was purified with column chromatography on silica gel (200–300 mesh) to afford the title compound.
